self_critique:
Overall assessment

The run found a modest improvement from 0.6018 to 0.604247, but the search was too bundled and stopped too early to establish why it improved or whether the gain is robust.

What was suboptimal

- Node 001 changed nearly everything at once: architecture, objective, regularization, optimizer, schedule, recency weighting, checkpointing, and seed ensembling. This prevents attribution and makes the stated overfitting diagnosis largely unfalsifiable.
- Node 002 compounded the problem with another large composite: sequence history, multiple context features, auxiliary supervision, and ensembling. Its actual gain was only about 0.0008, far below the predicted 0.0024.
- The policy’s hypotheses were more confident than the evidence warranted. Node 001 claimed validation-overfit behavior, while node 003 later admitted that the relevant learning curve was unavailable.
- Uncertainty was not handled consistently. Only the baseline reports sigma, and it is unclear whether later improvements exceed seed-to-seed or split variance. Rank-averaging five seeds at node 001 and mean logits from two at node 002 also confound modeling gains with ensemble gains.
- Node 003 was a reasonable isolated objective test, but one failed mutation was treated as convergence. The rejection only shows that this particular centered-BCE formulation did not help the current stack.
- Repeated decisions on one validation set risk adaptive validation overfitting, especially when gains are below 0.001.

What I would change in the scaffold

- Require paired, fixed-seed comparisons and report mean, standard deviation, and confidence interval for every accepted node.
- Separate single-model improvements from ensembling. Search with one seed first; evaluate a predeclared ensemble only at the end.
- Limit each node to one conceptual intervention, or require an ablation matrix for composite proposals.
- Require evidence for diagnoses such as overfit, underfit, or objective mismatch: train/validation curves, checkpoint trajectory, and metric decomposition.
- Compare predictions as well as scores: correlation, per-user/slate performance, cold-start slices, and recency/activity slices.
- Use an untouched confirmation split for finalists.
- Do not declare convergence after one rejection when the latest accepted node has not been ablated.

What the next run should try first

Start from node 002 and perform a controlled ablation using identical seeds and training settings. First compare:

1. Node 001 plus causal author-history sequence only.
2. Node 001 plus context features only.
3. Node 001 plus watch-time auxiliary loss only.
4. The full node 002 model.
5. Each model without ensemble averaging.

This will identify whether the small node 002 gain is real and which component produces it. If only one experiment can be run first, test the causal author-history sequence alone: it is the most structurally distinct addition and the likeliest source of complementary signal. Do not retry the node 003 objective unchanged; revisit listwise or pairwise losses only after measuring slate structure and metric alignment.
